items.title: fix(tui): scope MCP startup status by thread

observed_change: Codex adds nullable `threadId` ownership to app-server MCP startup notifications and routes TUI MCP startup diagnostics to the owning thread.
evidence: The app-server protocol struct and generated schema add nullable `threadId` to `McpServerStatusUpdatedNotification`.
The app-server README documents `threadId` as the owning thread id or null for app-scoped startup.
TUI notification targeting now routes MCP startup notifications to a thread or treats missing `threadId` as `AppScoped`.
The PR body and tests describe subagent MCP failures staying out of the parent transcript while remaining visible in the child thread.
candidate_followups: Check Decodex app-server protocol handling for MCP startup notifications and update exhaustive schemas if needed.
Use thread-scoped MCP startup events as ownership evidence in Control Plane diagnostics once Decodex consumes this upstream protocol shape.
Keep null `threadId` behavior explicit in operator-facing docs to avoid routing app-scoped lifecycle events to the active thread.
social_notes: Public copy should mention both the app-server field and the user-visible parent-transcript noise fix.
Warn strict app-server clients to accept the new nullable field.
caveats: The TUI currently ignores app-scoped null MCP startup notifications because there is no app-level target.
Missing `threadId` remains deserializable for compatibility, but generated strict clients may still need updates.
